external_primary.title: Instruct-FD: Can Your Full-Duplex Speech System Follow Turn-Taking Instructions?
external_primary.admitted_takeaway: Use explicit turn-management instructions as an independent experimental variable instead of scoring only generic duplex behavior. Compare the same conversational stimulus under different requested turn-taking behavior and measure whether the system changes its response appropriately.

observed_packet_controls: VoiceOutputPacket carries speech_act and playback/cancellation state
accept_input invokes cancel_for_barge_in when barge_in is true
current_f2_static_observation.observed_policy_binding_gap_candidate: In the inspected packet schemas there is no explicit per-turn turn-policy identifier/reference. This is a static observation only; it does not prove that policy is absent system-wide because an upstream component may legitimately compile policy into barge_in/speech_act/provenance before packets reach this layer.

hypothesis: For a full-duplex system to claim instruction-conditioned turn management, an A/B trace should be able to prove which requested turn policy governed each tested turn and show a policy-sensitive behavioral difference without changing the underlying user stimulus or causal identity lineage.
counterhypothesis: The packet cortex is intentionally policy-agnostic and a current upstream authority already binds the requested policy strongly enough that packet-level behavior can be audited without adding any new packet field. If that binding exists and the A/B trace passes, no product mutation is warranted.

benchmark_discriminator.name: PFD_POLICY_CONDITIONED_AB_V1
benchmark_discriminator.principle: Hold session/turn stimulus, timing and packet content constant while changing only an explicitly identified turn-management directive at the admitted upstream policy surface.
cases: PFD1 overlap-yield A/B: identical overlap stimulus under a directive that permits continuing versus one that requires yielding/acknowledging; record exact policy identity and resulting cancellation/output trace
PFD2 backchannel A/B: identical non-final listening stimulus under quiet-listen versus backchannel-permitted directive; record whether output/event behavior changes only with policy
PFD3 proactive-interruption A/B: identical semantic stimulus under no-proactive-interruption versus explicitly permitted proactive intervention; require exact causal/policy provenance
PFD4 determinism replay: same exact policy identity plus same packet stimulus must reproduce the same deterministic packet/event decision trace at this surrogate layer

PFD5 provenance falsifier: if a claimed policy-conditioned trace cannot bind an exact policy identity/reference to the tested turn, classify the claim as EVIDENCE_INVALID rather than inferring policy compliance
benchmark_discriminator.success_condition: Either identify an existing exact policy-binding surface and produce policy-conditioned A/B evidence, or demonstrate a bounded missing-binding condition that can be handed to Trigger4 without redesigning the voice stack.

nonduplication_fences: Do not mutate F2-WP-900 G4 or duplicate its current causal runtime intervention/readback work.
Do not duplicate the active recovery-checkpoint bounds falsifier.
Do not duplicate the microturn presence_state diagnostic/frontier.
Do not reopen generic ASR/TTS/model scouting.
Do not reuse the existing PACKET_CORTEX_CAUSAL_TURN_IDENTITY_FALSIFIER semantic claim as mutation authority.

routing.trigger4_handoff_condition: Only after fresh ownership resolution and either an executable PFD failure with exact policy binding or proof that no admitted upstream policy identity can be bound for an intended instruction-conditioned path.
routing.preferred_first_action: Search current source/tests for an admitted turn-policy binding/consumer and execute PFD1-PFD5 against that existing surface before proposing code.
